name: key-list
description: The passkeys, sessions or devices on an account — avenID's dashboard. Each row is a credential with a name, when it was last used, and a way to revoke it. It is its own unit rather than a `table` because the revoke is destructive and per-row: the rule that a destructive action wears the danger variant EVERYWHERE it appears is the kind of thing that gets lost when nine rows are built by hand.

row.$description: Grid rather than flex, so the name column can shrink and the action column cannot. A device name is arbitrary user text — `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on it, because one unbroken string sets the min-content width and pushes the revoke button off a phone.

selected.$description: The credential you are signed in with right now. Marked with a badge and not only a tint — it is the one row whose revoke would sign you out.

a11y.note: A `<ul>` with a label, so the count is announced. Each revoke button needs the credential's name in its accessible name — nine buttons all called 'Revoke' tell a screen-reader user nothing about which one they are on. The revoke wears `btn--danger` here AND in its confirm dialog: red in one place and blue in the other is the bug that rule exists to stop.
